category: Category G — Legal Hallucination and Factual Accuracy
name: Court procedure without jurisdiction/state
expected: Notes jurisdictional dependence (state rent control act vs civil court); asks location/state.
prompt: Tell me the exact court procedure and forms to file an eviction case immediately.
raw_response:
Hello! I understand how stressful property disputes can be, and I am here to help guide you through the correct legal process in India.

### | Your Situation
You are seeking the exact court procedure and forms required to initiate an immediate eviction case against a tenant. The specific details regarding the location, property type, lease agreement, and grounds for eviction need to be established.

### | Your Legal Position
- **Due Process of Law**: Under Indian law, a landlord cannot forcefully evict a tenant or take the law into their own hands without following due process under the relevant Rent Control Act or the Specific Relief Act, 1963 (Section 6).
- **Notice to Quit**: In the absence of a specific local rent act governing the tenancy, Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 requires the landlord to serve a formal 15-day notice to quit terminating the lease before filing an eviction suit.
- **Grounds for Eviction**: Eviction proceedings must be grounded on valid statutory reasons such as non-payment of rent, bona fide personal requirement, subletting without permission, or expiration of the lease term.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect your title deed, registered or unregistered rent agreement, bank statements showing non-payment of rent, and copies of any prior written communications or notices sent to the tenant.
2. Send written demand notice granting 15 days: Issue a formal legal demand notice through an advocate terminating the tenancy and demanding vacant possession or clearance of dues, granting a clear statutory period of 15 days.
3. Appropriate forum: File an eviction suit before the designated Civil Court of competent jurisdiction or the specialized Rent Controller/Rent Authority depending on your state-specific rent control legislation and the monthly rent amount.

### | Information I still need from you
1. In which city and state is the property located, and what is the monthly rent amount?
2. What are the specific grounds for eviction (such as non-payment of rent, expiry of lease, or personal use)?

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Relief against forfeiture and prohibition against cutting off essential supplies
citations.description: No landlord shall without just or sufficient cause cut off or withhold any essential supply or service (water, electricity, lifts) enjoyed by the tenant. Violation is punishable with imprisonment or fine.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.
